text:
The closest match among the listed options is "Medium: law as written statutes; institution: law as enforced by the police and the executive." It fits only loosely. Habermas's law as medium is positive, statutory law used as a steering code by the administrative and economic systems. His law as institution is law rooted in the lifeworld and legitimated by communicative action, which the executive-enforcement wording doesn't capture. I'm choosing it only because the other option (media and courts) fits worse.

CONFIDENCE: 55
